rows.text: The single most important rule to understand is that you still own and control all Equipment and Auras attached to Alexios even when opponents take control of him. When an opponent attacks another opponent with Alexios and connects, triggered abilities on your equipment—such as drawing two cards from Mask of Memory, untapping all your lands from Sword of Feast and Famine, or harvesting stockpiles of Treasures from The Reaver Cleaver—trigger for YOU, not the attacking player. Crucially, commander damage is tied to the physical card: all 21 lethal points can be dealt across opponents' turns, turning Alexios into a 4-attacks-per-round freight train that forces opponents to eliminate each other while fueling your hand and mana pool.

Prioritize hands with two or three lands and fast mana (Sol Ring, Lotus Petal, Simian Spirit Guide, Rite of Flame, or rituals) to deploy Alexios on turn 1 or turn 2. Having at least one piece of equipment (Commander's Plate, Mask of Memory, Beamtown Beatstick, or Two-Handed Axe) ready to attach on turn 2 or 3 ensures Alexios begins snowballing commander damage immediately.

Deploy Alexios early and pass him around the table. Let opponents take the wheel and hit each other for 4, 5, 6, and 7 commander damage while your equipment draws cards and generates Treasures for you.

Drop stax pieces (Trinisphere, Defense Grid, Cursed Totem) to prevent opponents from executing their own gameplans. If the game reaches turn 6 and opponents try to hide behind blockers, resolve Dualcaster Mage with Twinflame or Aggravated Assault with Sword of Feast and Famine to close out the table.
